name: Geostationary Orbit
story: Exactly 35,786 km up — the altitude where an orbit takes exactly 24 hours, so the satellite hangs motionless over a fixed longitude on the equator. Weather satellites stare at the same continent forever; communications satellites paint a dish-sized footprint and never move. There are no parking spaces, only parking slots — each operator gets a longitude band assigned by the ITU.
comparison: About 1/11th of the way to the Moon. A round-trip TV signal via GEO comsat takes ~240 ms — long enough to hear on a phone call ("satellite delay").
